notes: 1919 company mark surviving only as a screened 1974 catalogue cover (halftone, off-square, extra place-arc) and a low-contrast etch on brushed stainless; TWO further marks also survive only as artefacts — the works proving stamp as a die impression struck into a steel test coupon (near-value struck metal, a burnished burr halo that fattens the glyph, an empty inspector number box that must knock out, and it only ever reproduces at ~9mm so it closes at strike size), and the 1919 cast heritage device as a raking-light photo of a green-on-green painted casting (the only edge signal is the cast shadow, not the metal, and the shallow draft doubles strokes); last year's plate PDF set as one continuous story; a 14-machine order book with one over-long designation and a duplicated serial. One system of three marks, four physical media, no mark a rescaled copy of another.

assets.prompt: Flatbed scan of a 1974 industrial parts-catalogue cover, printed in ONE deep charcoal ink on aged cream board. The company mark is printed LARGE and centred: a compound lockup with a central geometric monogram of the letters R M W enclosed in a bold ring, and around the outside of the ring an ARC of small-caps place type reading 'REDECKER MACHINE WORKS  SHEBOYGAN  WISCONSIN', separated from the ring by a thin hairline rule. Critically, the whole mark is printed through a COARSE HALFTONE SCREEN typical of 1974 offset: at scan resolution every ink edge is a visible field of dots and rosette moire rather than a clean solid line, so the geometry looks solid from a distance but breaks into stipple up close. The cream board is scanned slightly OFF SQUARE (rotated about 3 degrees) with a faint drop shadow along one edge, subtle paper grain and foxing, flat even scanner light. Below the mark, small screened body type: 'PARTS CATALOGUE  No. 41  1974'. Understated, mechanical, industrial. No modern styling.
assets.defect_engineered: coarse halftone screen (trace receives a field of dots, returns lumpy stippled geometry); outer place-name arc the nameplate version lacks; board scanned off square (needs straightening)

assets.prompt: Handheld smartphone photograph, taken at a slight angle, of a brushed stainless-steel machine data nameplate bolted to a rebuilt industrial press. The company mark is ETCHED into the steel (no ink at all): a laser/acid etch of a central geometric monogram of the letters R M W inside a bold ring with a thin hairline rule, small-caps lettering inside the ring, and NO outer place-name arc (this version is simpler than the printed one). Because it is a bare etch, the mark and the brushed-metal ground sit at NEARLY THE SAME VALUE with very low contrast, and the horizontal BRUSH GRAIN of the stainless runs right across the plate so the grain lines read almost as strongly as the etched lines. Four hex bolts at the corners, faint fingerprints and workshop dust, uneven overhead shop lighting with a soft specular sheen across the metal. Realistic, slightly imperfect real-world snapshot, not a studio shot.
assets.defect_engineered: etch on brushed stainless (mark and ground near-equal value, low contrast; brush grain competes with the etch; enclosed ring interior that a one-call knockout returns as a solid disc)

assets.prompt: Extreme close-up handheld macro photograph of a small round works PROVING STAMP struck by a hardened steel die into a polished mild-steel test coupon (a thumb-sized offcut). The struck device is a compound mark: an outer struck ring carrying the small-caps words 'REDECKER PROVED' following the ring, a central bend-angle glyph (a stylised formed-sheet vee, two short strokes meeting at an obtuse angle), and beneath the glyph a small empty rectangular box where an inspector hand-stamps the proving number (the box is BLANK in the die, no number). Critically, because the stamp is STRUCK METAL there is NO ink at all and the impression sits at nearly the same value as the polished steel ground, and around the whole impression there is a raised BURNISHED BURR where the die displaced the metal, a bright ragged halo that reads almost as strongly as the struck lines themselves. The coupon carries fine circular machining swirl, a faint second GHOST STRIKE offset by a hair where the die bounced, light oil smears and a thumbprint, and hard raking workshop light from the upper left that throws the burr into glare on one side and shadow on the other. Realistic, imperfect, real-world macro snapshot, not a studio product shot.
assets.defect_engineered: struck steel, no ink (mark and polished ground near-equal value, exactly the etch problem again but on a new object); a raised burnished burr halo rings the impression and reads as part of the glyph, so the isolation that takes the mark fattens it and closes the bend-angle vee apex and the ring's inner counter into a blob at the ~9mm size it actually strikes into a plate corner, while the isolation that ducks the burr thins the ring rule and number-box outline away; the inspector's number box is BLANK in the die and must be recovered as an OPEN knockout, not a filled square; a faint offset ghost strike doubles some lines; only ever reproduces small, so a version that looks correct at coupon scale fails at strike size reversed on Works Green

assets.prompt: Raking-light handheld photograph of a raised CAST heritage badge on the main frame casting of an industrial press, the badge cast in relief directly into the iron and then painted over in the works deep green (#33564A) exactly like the rest of the frame, so it is a GREEN-ON-GREEN raised emblem with no colour difference at all between the badge and the field around it. The badge reads 'FORMED TRUE 1919 SHEBOYGAN' in cast small-caps around a small central anvil-and-brake device. It is lit by hard workshop light raking from the upper right, so the ONLY thing separating the badge from the field is the directional shadow the relief throws: a bright lit ramp on the upper-right side of every raised stroke and a dark cast shadow on the lower-left, with the flat green field identical in value to the flat tops of the raised letters. The casting has a shallow DRAFT ANGLE so each raised stroke has a soft sloping side rather than a crisp wall, plus chips of old paint, a little surface rust caught in the shadow, and a soft specular sheen across the paint. Realistic, imperfect, real-world snapshot at a slight angle, not a studio shot.
assets.defect_engineered: raised painted cast relief, green-on-green (badge and field identical in value; the ONLY edge signal is the directional side-light shadow, so a value/threshold isolation catches the SHADOW offset from the true casting edge and returns an emblem shifted and fattened toward the lit side); the shallow draft ramp on each stroke reads as a second edge so a naive trace double-lines the strokes; must recover the casting edge, not the cast shadow, and it sits as a SECONDARY mark beside the company mark on the bay-door sign, never carrying the outer place arc

LAYOUT DESCRIPTION (for the renderer/author of this press PDF)

Page: US Letter, 8.5 x 11 in portrait. A single data plate is centred on the page; the plate artwork is approx 150 x 90 mm landscape. No bleed is set (and none can be introduced from this file).

Plate appearance: solid Works Green (#33564A) field with the recovered mark reversed (Signal White) in the top-left corner and the works address block reversed beneath a hairline rule at the bottom.

VARIABLE WORDING — SET AS ONE CONTINUOUS THREADED TEXT STORY (a single text frame / one flow), NOT as six separate labelled frames. The lines run consecutively inside that one story, each reading 'LABEL   value':
  MODEL        <model>
  SERIAL NO.   <serial>
  YEAR         <year>
  VOLTAGE      <voltage> V
  PHASE        <phase>
  WEIGHT (kg)  <weight>

The MODEL line sits in a FIXED-MEASURE frame sized to the longest 2024 designation; a longer designation does NOT spill, reflow or overset, it simply stops drawing at the frame's right edge.

FIXED address block beneath the story (not variable):
  REDECKER MACHINE WORKS
  1419 Foundry Street, Sheboygan, WI 53081 USA

Example values shown on last year's plate:
  MODEL RB-90 | SERIAL NO. RMW-259114 | YEAR 2024 | VOLTAGE 480 V | PHASE 3 | WEIGHT (kg) 4600

Type: flat mechanical grotesque, high contrast, widely letterspaced, Signal White reversed out of Works Green.
assets.defect_engineered: variable plate wording authored as ONE continuous story (converted frames won't match the 6 tidy printed blocks; a lossy readout can drop a run and keep its line break); MODEL line is a fixed-measure frame that truncates instead of overrunning

assets.content:
REDECKER MACHINE WORKS — WORKS STANDARDS
(for the mark recovery and the November plate run)

THE MARK
Carried on every machine since 1919. One mark, reproduced flat, mechanical, high contrast, generously spaced. Never heritage or distressed, never a thin consumer-tech geometric sans. Weight and spacing do the work.

WORKS GREEN — as the paint shop mixes it
  HEX 33564A | RGB 51 86 74 | CMYK 70 30 45 55 | approx PMS 5535 C
  This is the FIELD colour. The mark reverses out of it clean, including the enclosed interior of the ring.
Other colours
  Machine Black  HEX 1B1E1D   (the one-colour stamp)
  Plate Steel    HEX 8A9091
  Cream Board    HEX E8E2D2
  Signal White   HEX F6F6F3   (reversed wording on plates)

ADDRESS BLOCK (must read exactly, on every plate)
  REDECKER MACHINE WORKS
  1419 Foundry Street, Sheboygan, WI 53081, USA
  +1 920 555 0147

REQUIRED PLATE WORDING (every data plate carries, in this order)
  MODEL
  SERIAL NO.
  YEAR
  VOLTAGE
  PHASE
  WEIGHT (kg)
  ...then the works address block beneath a hairline rule.
All plate wording reversed (Signal White) out of Works Green, flat mechanical grotesque, widely letterspaced.

VARIANTS REQUIRED FROM THE RECOVERED MARK
  1. Master (full colour)
  2. One-colour (Machine Black) for the invoice stamp
  3. Reversed knockout out of Works Green (ring interior must knock out, not fill)
  4. Single closed-outline cut file for the laser house (bay-door sign)
All four off ONE geometry.

THE OTHER TWO MARKS WE CARRY (recover these too, each its OWN geometry)
  A. THE WORKS PROVING STAMP
     Struck into every finished machine after its load test, and printed small on the test certificate. A small ROUND device: a struck ring reading 'REDECKER PROVED' around a central bend-angle glyph (a formed-sheet vee), with a small OPEN box beneath the glyph where the inspector hand-stamps the proving number. It strikes at about 9 mm, so it has to hold the vee apex and the ring counter at THAT size, and the number box must stay OPEN (knock out), never fill solid, so the inspector's figures read. Recover it from the die impression on the test coupon. The engraver needs it as artwork he can cut a die from.
  B. THE 1919 CAST HERITAGE DEVICE
     Cast in relief into the main frame casting and carried on the bay-door sign BESIDE the company mark. Reads 'FORMED TRUE 1919 SHEBOYGAN' around a small anvil-and-brake device. On the frames it is painted the works green over the raised casting, so the only version we hold is a raking-light photograph where the edge is the CAST SHADOW, not the metal. Recover the casting edge, not the shadow. It is a SECONDARY mark: it never competes with the company mark and never carries the outer place arc.
  Neither of these is the company mark and neither is decoration lifted off it. THREE marks, three separate recoveries, one variant family only WITHIN each mark.

NOTE FROM THE FLOOR
Whichever surviving source is used, the current company mark is the one WITHOUT the outer place-name arc (the 1974 catalogue added the arc; the machines do not carry it).
